reason: In Exodus 5:21 (present in this text), the Israelite overseers encounter Moses and Aaron and voice clear criticism against their leaders, saying: 'יֵרֶא יְהוָה עֲלֵיכֶם וְיִשְׁפֹּט אֲשֶׁר הִבְאַשְׁתֶּם אֶת־ רֵיחֵנוּ בְּעֵינֵי פַרְעֹה וּבְעֵינֵי עֲבָדָיו לָתֶת־ חֶרֶב בְּיָדָם לְהָרְגֵנוּ' (May Yahweh look upon you and judge, because you have made our scent repulsive in the eyes of Pharaoh and his servants, giving them a sword to kill us). Additionally, Moses himself (a leader of the people) voices criticism/questioning of Yahweh in Exodus 5:22-23, asking why Yahweh has brought trouble upon the people and failed to deliver them. Both elements of the statement are satisfied: the Hebrew people criticize their leaders, and a leader criticizes Yahweh.
